facts.statement: The genus Cerebavis was described by Kurochkin and colleagues in 2006.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Kurochkin et al., 2006

facts.statement: The animal is known from a single partial skull found in the Melovatskaya Formation of the Volgograd Region in Russia.
facts.quote: known from a single partial skull (PIN 5028/2) found in the Melovatskaya Formation of Volgograd Region in Russia

facts.statement: The fossil was initially misidentified as a fossilized brain of an enantiornithean bird.
facts.quote: The skull was initially described as the fossilised brain of an enantiornithean by Russian palaeornithologist Evgeny Kurochkin and colleagues in 2006

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers reinterpreted the fossil as an incomplete and abraded skull rather than a brain cast.
facts.quote: In 2011 the fossil was reinterpreted as an incomplete and heavily abraded skull rather than a fossilised brain

facts.statement: A 2015 reappraisal by the original authors concluded the specimen belonged to an ornithurine rather than an enantiornithean.
facts.quote: In 2015, a detailed reappraisal of the specimen by the same authors concluded that it belonged to an ornithurine instead of an enantiornithean and revised its diagnosis

facts.statement: Cerebavis lived during the middle Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: lived during the middle Cenomanian of the Late Cretaceous period

facts.statement: The animal lived between 99.6 and 93.5 million years ago during the middle Cenomanian.
facts.quote: vivió durante la época del Cenomaniense medio (Cretácico superior, hace 99,6 - 93,5 Ma)

facts.statement: Cerebavis is classified within the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the suborder Theropoda.
facts.quote: subordo: Theropoda

facts.statement: Cerebavis is placed in the unranked family Avialae.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Avialae

facts.statement: The animal is classified within the unranked genus Ornithurae.
facts.quote: unranked_genus: Ornithurae

facts.statement: The parent group of Cerebavis is Ornithurae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithurae

facts.statement: A 2021 redescription of Borogovia suggested Cerebavis might be a scansoriopterygid located at the base of the non-avian Oviraptorosauria clade.
facts.quote: En 2021, una redescripción de Borogovia encontró que era un posible escansoriopterígido, que se ubica en la base del clado no aviano Oviraptorosauria

facts.statement: The animal was identified as an ornithurine due to the lack of a postorbital bone, thin skull roof, and high fusion between skull bones.
facts.quote: Cerebavis was reidentified as an ornithurine as it seemingly lacked a postorbital bone and consequently a temporal bar dividing the temporal fenestra, as well as the thinness of the skull roof and the high degree of fusion between the bones of the skull

facts.statement: The brain structure resembles that of living birds, lacking a large pineal gland and having olfactory bulbs of expected size.
facts.quote: The brain more closely resembles that of living birds than originally interpreted by Kurochkin and colleagues, lacking a large pineal gland and with olfactory bulbs of expected size compared to living birds

facts.statement: Despite its advanced shape, the animal seemingly lacked a wulst, suggesting its brain was not fully modern.
facts.quote: Notably though, despite its advanced size and shape Cerebavis seemingly lacked a wulst, a structure found in the brains of modern birds, suggesting its brain was not fully modern

facts.statement: The brain shows unusual characteristics, including a well-developed olfactory system and a large cerebrum.
facts.quote: muestra algunas características inusuales, incluido un sistema olfativo bien desarrollado y un cerebro grande

facts.statement: The brain could show a relatively large parietal eye and pineal gland.
facts.quote: el cerebro de Cerebavis cenomanica podría mostrar un ojo parietal y una glándula pineal relativamente grandes

facts.statement: In 2011, the specimen was regarded as potentially a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2011 the fossil was reinterpreted as an incomplete and heavily abraded skull rather than a fossilised brain, and regarded Cerebavis as a probable non-enantiornithean bird and potentially a nomen dubium

facts.statement: It is debated whether the animal is an ornithurine or a scansoriopterygid at the base of non-avian Oviraptorosauria.
facts.quote: En 2021, una redescripción de Borogovia encontró que era un posible escansoriopterígido, que se ubica en la base del clado no aviano Oviraptorosauria
